subject: Lease the eager-judge mark on dispatch so concurrent loops don't double-judge a node
description:
Prerequisite for loop-as-default (many concurrent request-scoped loops). Today the eager mark is cleared too late (at pull, not dispatch) and decideOne emits the directive via a pure read with no claim — so two concurrent loops double-dispatch and double-judge a node.

THE RACE (traced in code):
- routes/judge.js /judge/next?node= (~line 56-71): buildQueueForNode(node) returns the node's edges by judged:false, then clearEagerJudge(node) clears the MARK — but only when a judge PULLS. The edges stay judged:false until verdicts post.
- daemon.js decideOne emits action:'judge_eager' from a pure read (lib/judge.js eagerJudgeNodes prunes RESOLVED marks but does NOT claim PENDING ones).
- So: Loop A decideOne emits judge_eager(X); before A's judge pulls, Loop B decideOne ALSO emits judge_eager(X); both dispatch; A pulls + clears mark; B pulls — buildQueueForNode(X) still returns X's unjudged edges (mark gone but edges still judged:false) → both judge the same edges.
- Severity: not corruption (keep-apply ~idempotent), but wasted judge spawns (cost + mis-attributes /24 per-node accounting), nondeterminism if A/B disagree (last-write-wins), and DOUBLE journal rows for one edge (skews keep-rate analytics).

FIX — lease-on-dispatch, not clear-on-pull:
1. When the eager directive is DISPATCHED (decideOne emits judge_eager, or the orchestration layer claims it), CLAIM the mark: change overlay.eagerJudge[node] from a bare epoch to {epoch, dispatchedAt, leaseTtlMs} (or a parallel lease map). A concurrent decideOne / eagerJudgeNodes SKIPS a node whose lease is still live. The lease TTL re-opens the node if that judge dies (mirror the existing stale-claim/reset pattern from task D / the task-claim reaper).
2. Belt-and-suspenders idempotency: /judge/verdict (routes/judge.js) should NO-OP a verdict for an edge that is no longer judged:false (already kept/pruned this pass) — so even a double-pull can't double-journal. Guard before appendVerdict + the keep/prune apply.
3. Keep the daemon dumb: it just leases + serves; the orchestration layer dispatches.

TEST: two simulated concurrent decideOne calls for the same marked node — only ONE gets judge_eager(node); the other skips (lease live); after lease TTL with no verdict, the node re-opens; a second /judge/verdict for an already-judged edge is a no-op (no second journal row). Run judge-eager + judge-verdict + judging-gate suites; git-stash to confirm pre-existing sandbox failures predate you.

Files: lib/overlay.js (eagerJudge value shape + lease/clear helpers), lib/judge.js (eagerJudgeNodes/eagerJudgePending skip-leased + lease accessor), daemon.js decideOne (claim on emit), routes/judge.js (verdict idempotency guard; reconcile clearEagerJudge at pull with the lease). Daemon restart to go live — NOTE it, do NOT restart (gated).

summary: MERGE PENDING — orch/attempt/091a4bf1-b671-4ff9-854d-993775faa5ee-27: Added eagerJudgeLease overlay field to prevent concurrent heartbeat loops from double-dispatching the same eager-judge node. acquireEagerJudgeLease/clearEagerJudgeLease in lib/overlay.js; eagerJudgeNodes() in lib/judge.js skips leased nodes; eagerJudgeDirective() in daemon.js acquires leases for all dispatched nodes; routes/judge.js clears lease when eagerJudge mark is cleared on /judge/next?node=. 16 new tests in test/judge-eager-lease.test.js, all passing. Existing judge-eager.test.js updated (28 pass). Full suite: 102/113 pass (same pre-existing failures as main).
